thread.title: Should Apple Buy Tesla? - Barron's

author: Teresa Rivas
title: Should Apple Buy Tesla? - Barron's
text:
By Teresa Rivas April 20, 2018 3:50 p.m. ET Shares of Tesla (TSLA) are down again Friday, as investors debate whether the stock's next move will be to $200 or $400 , depending on Model 3 demand and production .
Illustration: Bloomberg News Bernstein's A.M. (Toni) Sacconaghi, Jr. takes a look at the stock on Friday, parsing a host of issues that investors have posed in recent weeks, from its debt (perhaps an issue if the stock continues to decline) to expansion in China (potentially a long-term positive development, as the country is opening up more to foreign auto makers ).
Among these points, Sacconaghi also throws cold water on the hope that Tesla could be acquired by another car maker. Even with the stock's recent decline, its market cap and valuation make Tesla quite expensive, even for big original equipment manufacturers. Moreover, plenty of rival auto makers, who are already working on their own electric vehicles, may prefer to compete with rather than buy Tesla, as they're willing to bet that Tesla's lead in battery technology is temporary.
That said, just because it may be unlikely that another car maker may shy away from buying Tesla doesn't mean that the company's an unappealing acquisition target. After all, it has a valuable brand, a reputation as an innovator (which helps to attract top talent), and would offer plenty of synergies to an acquirer with manufacturing capabilities and capital to make highly desirable products.
So, if not another car maker, who might fit that bill? Apple (AAPL), proposes Sacconaghi, as it certainly has pockets deep enough to fund the deal and the operational capacity to overcome production problems. But don't get your hopes up: He doesn't think Apple is looking to make any big acquisitions--at least in the near future.
Tesla is down 3.1% to $290.70.
